parts.note: the first form any written work takes is the author's own handwritten or typed copy before printing

explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten or typed draft is the version of a book that exists before publication.

clue.text: The glow-worm revealed its proximity at Elsinore

definitions.text: The glow-worm revealed its proximity at Elsinore

parts.words: The glow-worm revealed its proximity at Elsinore
parts.note: in Hamlet, set at Elsinore, the Ghost says the glow-worm shows that morning is near, as its light pales

explanation.walkthrough: The Ghost in Hamlet leaves with 'The glow-worm shows the matin to be near'; the clue retells that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Matin is an old word for morning, the dawn the Ghost must flee.

parts.note: the cricket term 'popping crease' suggests that cloth with nothing 'popping' has no crease at all

explanation.surface: A fabric so smooth that nothing stands out in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The popping crease is the line a batsman stands behind in cricket; take away 'popping' and you are left with a fabric that does not crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Crease-resistant fabric keeps its shape and needs no ironing.

clue.text: Crisis due to collapse of boom at Portsmouth?

definitions.text: Crisis due to collapse of boom at Portsmouth?

parts.words: Crisis due to collapse of boom at Portsmouth?
parts.note: Southsea is a district of Portsmouth, and a boom that bursts is a bubble, so the question mark invites a local reading of a famous financial crash

explanation.surface: A naval town hit by a sudden economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1720 crash of the South Sea Company's shares is read as a bubble bursting at Southsea, the seaside part of Portsmouth on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1720 speculative mania in South Sea Company shares ended in a famous financial collapse.

parts.note: to return someone to a parliamentary seat is to vote them in, here for a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Voting a sitting member back in keeps them in the constituency they already held.

parts.note: daubing walls means coating them, and ... of Paris is the gypsum compound named after the city

explanation.surface: A vandal smears the walls of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city but the 'of Paris' in plaster of Paris, the material spread on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To coat a wall with a smooth paste is to render it with gypsum mortar.

parts.note: The Seven Year ... was a stage comedy about restlessness after seven years of marriage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a phase of life, which is also right: the urge to stray said to strike after seven years.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven-year urge for a change in a marriage is named after a restless irritation of the skin.

definitions.meaning: a goblin is a mischievous creature of Scandinavian folklore, like the giant dwelling under bridges
to fish here is a verb, trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a folklore monster and the method of angling by drawing a line through the water.

clue.text: Do they seize the chance to work on Sundays ?

definitions.text: Do they seize the chance to work on Sundays ?

parts.words: Do they seize the chance to work on Sundays ?
parts.note: the proverb tells farm workers to make hay while the sun shines, so Sundays reads as sunny days

explanation.surface: A question about labourers who grab Sunday overtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Sundays is to be read as sun days: the proverb says to make hay while the sun shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm hands cutting and drying grass in fine weather are the people the proverb is about.

clue.text: But it's run in the adjoining county

definitions.text: But it's run in the adjoining county

parts.words: But it's run in the adjoining county
parts.note: a horse race named after one English county is held at Newmarket racecourse in the next-door county of Suffolk

explanation.walkthrough: The Cambridgeshire is a handicap horse race at Newmarket, which lies just over the border in Suffolk; so the county's name is 'run' in its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn handicap at Newmarket carries the name of the neighbouring East Anglian county.

clue.text: Close shave that barely affects the poll

definitions.text: Close shave that barely affects the poll

parts.words: Close shave that barely affects the poll
parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, and a close shave of part of it leaves it bare

explanation.surface: A narrow escape in an election that hardly changed the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close shave' and 'poll' suggest a near thing in an election; poll is an old word for head, and 'barely' means leaving it bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks had the crown of the head shaved as a sign of religious life.

clue.text: One of Queen Mab's team shows science

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
in Romeo and Juliet Queen Mab is drawn by a team of little atomies, tiny beings

explanation.surface: A fairy's carriage horse turns out to be a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet has Queen Mab 'drawn with a team of little atomies'; one of them is an atomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of body structure is a branch of biological science.

parts.note: Sir John Franklin died in 1847 seeking the doubtful sea route through the Arctic above Canada

explanation.surface: A dubious bit of text that got the better of an American statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Franklin here is the Arctic explorer, not Benjamin; the sea route he sought was long suspected rather than proved.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea route over the top of North America was the explorers' great search.

clue.text: Just the stuff for the lightship

definitions.text: Just the stuff for the lightship

parts.words: Just the stuff for the lightship
parts.note: a lightship is a moored beacon vessel, but read as a light ship it wants a very light timber

explanation.walkthrough: Lightship reads as light ship: balsa is the very light wood of rafts like Kon-Tiki.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical timber is famously light and buoyant, used for rafts and models.

indicators.note: audible tells us the words for allure are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: allure is a bait, a lure drawing someone in

explanation.surface: A plea to turn down a seductive sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bait', something alluring, said out loud gives the word for lessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or subside is to grow smaller in strength.

clue.text: It's responsive and vocal against sham

parts.note: anti means against, opposed to
phony means fake or sham

explanation.surface: A claim that something is open and outspoken in opposing fakery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as praise for a campaigner; it is the call-and-response singing of a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate singing by two choirs answering each other is responsive vocal music.

clue.text: Make an end of white ant with sodium injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so sodium goes into the insect

parts.note: white ant is another name for a termite
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Killing off an insect pest with a shot of sodium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White ant' is the common name for the termite, which really is a pest you might kill; 'injection' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish or bring to a close is to stop it.

parts.note: amber is an English colour, a golden yellow
gris is French for grey

explanation.surface: Flags of Britain and France employed in making scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglo-French' gives one colour in each language, the English word first and then the French one; the scent material is grey, from whales.
explanation.definitionFit: The waxy substance from sperm whales is a prized fixative in scent-making.

parts.note: the line from Milton's Lycidas has a word missing before ears, which the solver supplies

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Lycidas reads 'Phoebus replied, and touch'd my trembling ears'; the gap is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective describes ears shaking with fear or awe.

clue.text: Vehement in the past for example

parts.note: the past is a tense of a verb, like present or future

explanation.surface: Someone was more passionate in former times, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The past' looks like history, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and fierce feeling is extreme in force.

clue.text: There's mischief in the air. Blame him!

definitions.text: There's mischief in the air. Blame him!

parts.words: There's mischief in the air. Blame him!
parts.note: airmen in the Second World War blamed unexplained mechanical faults on a mischievous imp

explanation.surface: Trouble is brewing and someone needs to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the air' sounds like a mood, but it is literal: RAF aircrews invented an imp to blame for faults in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary sprite was blamed by airmen for engine faults and other breakdowns.

clue.text: Great return gets points, or jeers

indicators.note: return means the word for great is turned back to front

parts.note: big means great
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A great comeback earns points, or boos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns BIG into GIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunts and mocking remarks are scornful jeers.

parts.note: to sound is to measure the depth of water with a weighted line, and the word for that is spoken like a stone fruit

explanation.walkthrough: Sound is a verb, measuring depth with a lead weight; that word is said like the name of a purple stone fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure water depth with a weighted line is to sound it.

definitions.meaning: to issue words is to say or express them
used before a noun, the word means complete, absolute, in the extreme

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to speak out and complete, as in total nonsense.

clue.text: Set high value on a rude stare perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A rude look might be prized, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RUDE STARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish something is to hold it dear and rate it highly.

parts.note: two French authors shared a surname, the father writing The Three Musketeers and the son La Dame aux camelias

explanation.walkthrough: Alexandre père and Alexandre fils were both French novelists with the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to both the elder novelist and his playwright son.

definitions.meaning: a bunting is a small seed-eating songbird
a table dainty is a delicacy for eating, here the bird served at a gourmet dinner

explanation.surface: Flags decorate a fine dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: The small European songbird is also a famous French gourmet delicacy.

definitions.note: the definition is a place found in Eire, so a noun phrase stands for a county name

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
trim means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: In Ireland a wreath of flowers is tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'In Eire': the answer is a county of the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The county in the north-west of the Republic lies within the Irish state.

parts.note: a tripod has three feet, and three feet is an imperial measure of length

explanation.walkthrough: Feet are both legs and units: three of them make the imperial length.
explanation.definitionFit: Three feet make up the imperial measure of thirty-six inches.

parts.note: runners are climbing vegetables as well as athletes, and a festive meal named after them is a party

explanation.walkthrough: Runners are runner beans, not athletes; a beano or celebratory meal is named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive meals or jolly celebrations are lively parties.
